I've been moderating this subverse for a few months, and figured it might be interesting to hear some stories from the people who subscribe to it (or from anyone!)

**My question is, how has kindness affected you? Has someone ever done a kindness for you, or a loved one? How did it make you feel? Conversely, have you ever done a kindness for someone else? How did that make you feel? Please share your stories, I'd love to hear them. **

I will start with mine.

Years ago, when my boyfriend (now husband) and I first began living together, we did not have much money. We made enough for rent and food and basic necessities, but anything else was difficult.

At around this same time, I lost my health insurance coverage.

I took (and still take) several medications, many of which allow me to function. The biggest one is migraine medicine, as I get severe, blinding migraines and can't work or really function when I have them. The medicine makes them stop. The medicine is also extremely expensive and is the only one that has worked for me.

One day, I went to the pharmacy to pick up a prescription. The pharmacist told me the cost of the medicine and I sighed, then replied that I would only be able to take 2 of the 9 pills I needed due to the cost.

I walked off as the pharmacist went to fill my prescription. When I returned, she pulled me to the side and told me that the woman behind me on line had heard me talking and had paid for my medicine.

It came out to $160.00. She paid for all of it. She did not want to be identified, but the pharmacist discreetly pointed her out. I came up to her, tears in my eyes, and thanked her for helping me. She did not seem like she was particularly well off (she looked to be middle class, though I guess appearances can be deceiving) and she told me that she had known what it was like to have hard times. I promised her that I would pay it forward.

Seven years have passed. I have a good job now, and I make decent money. Every year for the past 3 years I go to the pharmacy and give them 50$ to put towards people who cannot afford their medication. From what the pharmacist has told me, it's helped several people including two young mothers and an elderly woman. I feel it is the least I can do since I now have the means to do it. I will never forget that woman's actions; she proved to me that there was kindness in the world - that was the first time that I really saw it.
It's so nice to hear about good things people do for each other. It doesn't happen often enough, but when it does, it's nice.

It happens more than people think, I believe. I think a lot of times it is overlooked in favor of sadder stories. The harsher stories grab people's attention. That is not to say they don't deserve attention, but kindness and love deserves it as well. There are a lot of good people out there. Hopefully this subverse can let some of their stories be more known.
